questions.q: Why does the capstone plan disable the sa login rather than dropping it entirely?
options: It's kept as a tightly controlled, vaulted break-glass account for genuine emergencies, while being disabled for everyday use
sa cannot be dropped under any circumstances in SQL Server
Dropping sa would delete DispatchDB along with it
It's kept enabled and used daily by the DBA for convenience
questions.explain: sa is disabled day-to-day with its password rotated and vaulted, so it can still be used as a last resort, but it's no longer the account anything routine — including the application — logs in as.

questions.q: Why is dispatchtrack_svc granted db_datareader and db_datawriter on DispatchDB instead of being added to the sysadmin role?
options: Least privilege — the application only needs to read and write data in DispatchDB, not administer the entire instance the way the old sa-based connection effectively could
sysadmin membership is required for any application login to function at all
db_datareader and db_datawriter together are equivalent to sysadmin, so it makes no difference
SQL Server does not allow application logins to be granted sysadmin
questions.explain: Least privilege means granting exactly what's needed. The app needs to read and write rows in DispatchDB, not administer the server, so datareader/datawriter (plus execute rights) is the appropriate scope.

questions.q: What does the SQL Server Audit setup in this lesson specifically capture, and why does that matter for MERSQL01?
options: Successful and failed login attempts, written to a durable file, giving a record of access that previously didn't exist at all
Only query performance statistics, unrelated to security
A full backup of DispatchDB, taken automatically
It captures nothing until a DBA manually reviews the server every day
questions.explain: The SERVER AUDIT SPECIFICATION created here adds FAILED_LOGIN_GROUP and SUCCESSFUL_LOGIN_GROUP, giving MERSQL01 a durable, queryable trail of login activity where none existed before.

questions.q: Which single new job most directly fixes the runaway transaction log problem discovered in Lesson 64?
options: The DatabaseBackup - USER_DATABASES - LOG job, scheduled every 15 minutes
The DatabaseIntegrityCheck - USER_DATABASES job
The IndexOptimize - USER_DATABASES job
Disabling the sa login
questions.explain: In FULL recovery, only a log backup allows the log to be truncated and reused. Scheduling log backups every 15 minutes stops the log from growing without bound the way it did for six years.

questions.q: Ola Hallengren's scripts are described in this course as the 'industry standard' for maintenance. What gap on MERSQL01 do they close?
options: No index maintenance, no statistics updates, and DBCC CHECKDB never run — the scripts install jobs that handle backups, integrity checks, and index optimization on a schedule
They replace SQL Server Agent entirely with a third-party scheduler
They are only useful for Enterprise Edition and don't apply to MERSQL01's Standard Edition
They exist solely to manage login security, not maintenance
questions.explain: MERSQL01 had zero maintenance jobs beyond one disabled leftover. Ola Hallengren's standard job set (backup, integrity check, index optimize) fills exactly that gap using native SQL Server Agent jobs.
